title: Sort Even and Odd Indices Independently
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` indexed from 0. Rearrange it in two independent parts, leaving every value on an index of the same parity it started on:

- the values sitting at even indices (0, 2, 4, ...) are reordered among those positions from smallest to largest;
- the values sitting at odd indices (1, 3, 5, ...) are reordered among those positions from largest to smallest.

Return the resulting array.
notes:
## Intuition

The even positions and the odd positions never trade values, so they are really two separate little arrays woven together. Pull each one out, sort it the way its rule asks, and weave them back in place. One could also sort in place by swapping only same-parity positions, but that is a quadratic exchange sort; extracting and using a real sort is simpler and faster.

## Approach

1. Walk `nums` with index `i`; push values at even `i` onto `evens` and values at odd `i` onto `odds`.
2. Sort `evens` in ascending order and `odds` in descending order.
3. Build `result` by walking the indices again: even index `i` takes `evens[i / 2]`, odd index `i` takes `odds[(i - 1) / 2]`.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4, 1, 2, 3]` splits into `evens = [4, 2]` (indices 0 and 2) and `odds = [1, 3]` (indices 1 and 3). Sorting gives `evens = [2, 4]` and `odds = [3, 1]`. Weaving them back: index 0 gets 2, index 1 gets 3, index 2 gets 4, index 3 gets 1, so the answer is `[2, 3, 4, 1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the two sorts; the two passes are O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `evens`, `odds` and `result`.

## Pitfalls

- The two directions are opposite: even positions go up, odd positions go down. Swapping them is the most common bug.
- JavaScript's default `sort()` compares as strings (`10` before `9`); always pass a numeric comparator.
- Parity refers to the index, not to the value: an odd value at an even index belongs to `evens`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `evens` | values from even indices, later sorted ascending |
| `odds` | values from odd indices, later sorted descending |
| `i` | current index into `nums` and `result` |
| `result` | the rearranged array being built |
